A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PUP 3D-GS by the same authors. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support comparison despite changes in layout and experimental settings.

before.justification: v1 reports original pruning experiments, benchmark measurements, ablations and qualitative reconstructions in Sections 5–6 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark measurements, pruning-configuration sweeps, parameter ablations and qualitative reconstructions in Sections 5–6 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: Section 4.3 revises the reported patch-score computation from average-pooling blocks of rendered pixels to rendering downsampled images and evaluating their pixels. The central block-Fisher log-determinant score using Gaussian means and scales, followed by repeated pruning and refinement, remains unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine Mip-NeRF 360 scenes, truck and train from Tanks & Temples, and drjohnson and playroom from Deep Blending. Both also test pruning an EAGLES model of bicycle. Expanded ablations use scenes already represented in v1; no new task or domain is introduced.

E2.justification: v1 Tables 2–3 include both original one-round LightGaussian and LightGaussian (2×). v2 retains only the two-round configuration, now labeled LightGaussian, in these unquantized and quantized comparisons. This removes a comparator configuration rather than merely renaming both earlier entries.

E3.justification: The main protocol changes from 66% pruning twice, totaling 88.44%, to 80% then 50%, totaling 90%. Default patches change from 8×8 to 4×4, and rendering-speed hardware changes from RTX A5000 to RTX A4000. New sweeps use 5% two-round and 10% three-round pruning intervals, while several ablations expand to all Mip-NeRF 360 scenes. The main refinement budget remains 5,000 iterations per round.

E4.justification: v1's sparse pruning-percentage and round-count tests are expanded into schedule heatmaps, interpolated two-versus-three-round curves, and approximately 90% pruning comparisons in v2 Figures 3 and 6–8. v2 adds a rotation-parameter ablation and broadens the spatial/RGB and patch-size analyses. The direct pixel-versus-patch Spearman-correlation analysis in v1 Figure 3 is removed.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 6 adds standard-deviation bands around means computed through cubic interpolation across pruning configurations. These describe variability between settings, not uncertainty across independent training runs. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, random-seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Benchmark, quantization, per-scene and EAGLES results are extensively replaced under revised settings, alongside new ablation results. For example, Table 2 changes PUP's Mip-NeRF 360 PSNR/size from 26.83/86.29 MB to 26.67/74.65 MB. Quantized Tanks & Temples PSNR changes from PUP 21.81 versus LightGaussian 21.80 to 21.61 versus 21.88. These are changed-setting results, not direct performance gains or losses. Appendix SSIM rows remain unchanged despite revised main-table means.

T1.justification: v2 adds Appendix A.1 with a Gaussian-noise likelihood, regularity assumptions, a Laplace posterior approximation, a uniform-prior assumption and a proposed Fisher-log-determinant/entropy interpretation in Equations 11–15. This mathematical derivation is absent from v1. Equation 3 also corrects the compositing product's upper index from j-1 to i-1.

C1.justification: The same three core contributions remain. However, v2 strengthens the stated operating range: image-quality preservation after 80% first-round pruning replaces 66%, and the headline becomes 90% total pruning with 3.56× rendering speed rather than 88.44% with 2.65×. The abstract and introduction emphasize fidelity at higher compression ratios.

C2.justification: v2 adds geometric and memory-based explanations for excluding rotations, and favors two rounds for simplicity despite some three-round benefits at higher pruning percentages. Appendix A.1 adds an entropy interpretation. Section 7 replaces v1's general computational-overhead discussion with explicit N×36 Fisher-storage requirements and RTX A4000 feasibility, while retaining the converged-scene limitation.

D1.justification: v2 specifies a CUDA kernel for Hessian computation, whereas v1 only describes codebase integration and suggests optimized CUDA kernels as future work. It also documents 6×6 versus 10×10 Fisher matrices, their 2.78× storage difference, and the larger GPU required for the rotation variant. Hardware and patch defaults are updated; no new code or data access information is supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kirsch and Gal's work on Fisher information and information-theoretic quantities, and Lehmann and Casella's Theory of Point Estimation, supporting Appendix A.1. Existing references and the central positioning relative to LightGaussian, FisherRF, BayesRays and other compression methods are retained.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and substantial portions of the introduction, related work and method remain. v2 revises abstract and results prose, streamlines the background heading, renames Section 4.1, and reorganizes the appendices. Round-count and pruning-percentage discussions receive greater prominence in the main ablation section, while residual discussions are consolidated.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column formatting, with the teaser moved before the abstract. Qualitative panels are revised and enlarged, and supplementary visualizations receive dedicated pages. The correlation plot is removed, heatmaps and several line plots are added, and comparison and ablation tables are restructured.

improvement.justification: v2 provides more informative tests of pruning schedules and parameter choices, and makes probabilistic assumptions explicit. However, new reporting inconsistencies weaken confidence: its Table 8 retains v1's per-scene SSIM values, averaging 0.7920 for Mip-NeRF 360, while Table 2 reports 0.7862. Section 6.3 also says rotations reduce image quality although Table 5 reports higher PSNR with rotations, 26.79 versus 26.67. The added analytical value and unresolved reliability problems leave the net effect on overall quality uncertain.
